variant_decisions.evidence: ASV text reads 'I must needs glory' — an explicit rendering of the impersonal δεῖ. The variant δὴ ('Now') is relegated to the margin by the mapped textual note, 'Some ancient authorities read Now to glory is not expedient', which shows the Revisers knew the RP clause and did not print it.

ASV text has 'though it is not expedient' with no dative of person; RP συμφέρει μοι would require 'it is not expedient for me'. The mapped textual note carries the alternative clause to the margin, confirming the text is the impersonal συμφέρον μέν.
ASV text reads 'but I will come to visions', the adversative δὲ; γὰρ would give 'for I will come'. The mapped textual note assigns the whole RP form of the verse to the margin.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'save in my weaknesses' does not settle whether 'my' translates RP's μου or is supplied from the anaphoric article — the same verse-9 clause 'my power is made perfect' renders a base lemma δύναμις that carries no μου, so an unitalicized possessive is not a discriminator here.

Relative pronoun: rule 17 heads on the English token that most directly realizes the lexeme, which is the relativizer 'which'; 'that' is the supplied antecedent. Rule 22's head-on-the-nominal-word is scoped to a substantival article, not to a relative pronoun.
Supplied copula of the embedded predication whose predicate is the relative noun phrase, so it goes with the subject pronoun (rule 53); giving 'to be' to the relative remains defensible.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV text runs 'revelations, that I should not be exalted overmuch' with no connective, and the mapped textual note puts the other reading in the margin: 'Some ancient authorities read revelations—wherefore, that etc.' 'Wherefore' is διὸ, so the printed text is the omission.
Σατανᾶ and Σατᾶν are declensional variants of the same name; 'Satan' renders either.

ASV prints 'that I should not be exalted overmuch' twice, at the head and the close of the verse, so the second ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι stands in the text; the Tregelles omission would leave one clause only.

τελεῖται and τελειοῦται are alternative present passives of the same sense; 'is made perfect' renders either. The one mapped note is an alternative_rendering about 'spread a tabernacle over me' and decides nothing.
ASV 'glory in my weaknesses' leaves open whether 'my' renders μου or the possessive force of the article, exactly as at 12:9's 'my power' where the base lemma has no pronoun.

Rule 66: 'works' is a generic completion and 'mighty' carries the lexeme's sense, as EPH.5.5 'covetous man', JUD.1.12 'love feasts' and 2CO.8.16 'earnest care' do. Recorded medium because the corpus has no precedent for δύναμις rendered 'mighty work(s)' at all, and GAL.3.5 shows it willing to head a deed-rendering on the deed noun ('miracles'), so heading on 'works' remains defensible.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'by signs and wonders and mighty works' renders an instrumental dative, which is the ordinary English of both the bare dative and ἐν with the dative; the added preposition leaves no trace.
τε καὶ and bare καὶ are both Englished 'and'; 'signs and wonders and mighty works' does not show which the Revisers read.

ASV reads the singular 'jealousy' in a list whose plurals ('wraths', 'factions') are kept plural; RP's ζῆλοι would be 'jealousies'.
